_comment: GROUND TRUTH - ORBIN CONTRACTING LLC package (EMC Insurance, 07/15/25-07/15/26).
Built by reading all 271 real pages. Consumed by backend/scripts/score_gap_fill.py.
WHAT THIS FILE IS: {ACORD field name -> the value the declarations pages state}.
Everything at the top level without a leading underscore is SCORED. Every field
name below was validated against forms_schemas/ - a name that exists on no real
schema scores nothing and hides the gap it was meant to measure.
PACKAGE: 30 declarations/schedule pages inside 271. 11% signal, 89% standard-form
wording, and the ratio worsens through the package (17% / 9% / 8%) because every
added coverage part brings one dec page and dozens of wording pages.
FIVE parts: Inland Marine (6C7-40-02), Business Auto (6E7-40-02), Umbrella
(6J7-40-02), General Liability (BBC7263, a DIFFERENT carrier), plus the Common
Declarations. Property, Crime and Workers Comp are all stated 'No Coverage'.
_must_be_blank  boxes whose correct answer is EMPTY - the blank-over-wrong rule.
_not_scored     values with two or more equally correct printings; scoring them
would fail a right answer. Recorded, deliberately ungraded.
_traps          the specific printed sentences in THIS package that have already
produced client-reported wrong values.
_source_data    per-coverage-part values not yet mapped to a form field, kept for
the ACORD 131/141 fixtures. Values only - no commentary.
Page-by-page keep/drop classification and score_gap_fill's own limitations moved
to orbin_page_metadata.json on 2026-08-14: useful, but a different test.

terrorism_premium.note: THE SHARPEST FREQUENCY TRAP IN THE PACKAGE, now complete and confirmed. IL8383.2A is the SAME form printed three times - pages 5, 147 and 210 - and its SCHEDULE line carries a DIFFERENT value each time: 'Waived', '$34.00', '$31.00'. Three near-identical pages, three different right answers, distinguishable only by which coverage part's stack the page sits in. Any de-duplication that collapses repeated pages destroys two of the three; any frequency ranking picks whichever wording repeats most. Note also that $3, $31 and $34 are the three smallest money figures in the package and are decoys for every premium field - and that $31 is the only one of the four that also appears on a rating schedule (page 211), where it is a component of the $3,954 GL total.

gl_limits.source: page 205, 'General Liability Declarations', Form CG7000A Ed. 08-99, EMC Property & Casualty Company, 'Policy: BBC7263 - 26', term 07/15/2025-07/15/2026. All six are printed under one 'Limits of Insurance' heading, each with its qualifier. Page 148, the Umbrella's SCHEDULE OF UNDERLYING INSURANCE, independently confirms FOUR of the six - General Aggregate $2,000,000, Products-Completed Operations Aggregate $2,000,000, Personal and Advertising Injury $1,000,000, Each Occurrence $1,000,000 - and agrees exactly on all four. It does NOT restate damage-to-premises-rented or medical expense, which exist only on page 205.
gl_limits.restated_in_boilerplate: CG7759 (page 252) sections N and O restate '$500,000' and '$10,000' as the endorsement's own defaults - the SAME figures as the declarations. A benign coincidence, and the only place in 271 pages where a wording page happens to agree with a dec page. Do not mistake it for confirmation: it is a default that would print identically on a policy with different limits.

decoys.$3,000,000: page 143, COMMERCIAL UMBRELLA DECLARATIONS - the UMBRELLA's own limits, printed as three clean lines: 'Each Occurrence Limit (Liability Coverage)', 'Personal & Advertising Injury Limit', 'Aggregate Limit (Liability Coverage)'.

gl_limits.note: THE C23 DEFECT'S SOURCE, located, and part 3 makes it worse rather than better. There are now TWO pages titled DECLARATIONS carrying different 'Each Occurrence' limits - page 143 says $3,000,000 (umbrella) and page 205 says $1,000,000 (GL) - SIXTY-TWO PAGES APART. Nothing in the text distinguishes them except which coverage part's dec page you are standing on. That is page identity, and page identity is exactly what a single 175k-token prompt destroys. Chunking restores it.

gl_premium.source: page 205 ('Coverages Provided') and again on page 211 ('Total Estimated Policy Premium', GENERAL LIABILITY SCHEDULE, Form CG7001A Ed. 10-12)

full_component_breakdown_page_211.Location 000 - Fungi Or Bacteria Exclusi: ($33) - a CREDIT, printed in parentheses. The only negative number in 271 pages.

gl_premium.arithmetic: -33 + 150 + 1,305 + 1,198 + 803 + 500 + 31 = 3,954 EXACTLY. And the page-205 split reconciles to the same components: the $1,198 products line is class 91585's Products/Compl Ops column verbatim, and the other six sum to $2,756. SEVEN components, one of them negative, across two pages - the most demanding reconciliation in the package and the strongest single proof that both GL pages were read.
gl_premium.why_it_matters: A run that reads page 205 alone gets the right total from two clean lines. A run that reads page 211 alone can also get there, but only by summing seven numbers including a parenthesised credit that most numeric extractors will read as +33 rather than -33 - which lands on $4,020 and nothing on either page says $4,020.

_repeated_boilerplate.note: A MERGE defect, not a retrieval one - chunking will not fix it. Common interline forms attach to EVERY coverage part, so their text repeats once per part while a real declarations value is printed ONCE. `_merge_list_fields` ranks candidates on log1p(freq) + confidence, so the bias scales with the number of coverage parts. This package has five. CONFIRMED COUNTS across all 271 pages:

IL 71 68 Asbestos Exclusion.note: added on the re-audit - missed on the first pass

IL 74 51 Snow And Ice Plowing Exclusion.note: added on the re-audit. The only repeated form whose SCHEDULE box is filled in, identically, on both copies.

_repeated_boilerplate.verification: Every page number in the eight original entries was re-checked against the document on 2026-08-14 and every one is EXACT. The first pass got this table right; it was only incomplete. Four more repeated forms are added above, all of them 2 copies.
_repeated_boilerplate.the_arithmetic: log1p(1) = 0.693 for the $10,663 total premium, printed once. log1p(4) = 1.609 for the IL0017 boilerplate. The boilerplate scores 2.3x the real number on frequency alone, before confidence is even considered.
_repeated_boilerplate.recommendation: Worth its own fix after the harness produces a baseline. Options include damping frequency for text that appears in a known standard form, or scoring dec-page provenance rather than raw repetition. Do not touch it before there is a number to move.

CG 99 09 (pages 256-257).title: PREMIUM AUDIT NONCOMPLIANCE CHARGE
empty_boxes: Number Of Written Attempts To Obtain Audit Information: ___
CG 99 09 (pages 256-257).note: THE WORST TRAP IN 271 PAGES, and it is worse than every other blank form because the blank schedule is followed IMMEDIATELY, on the same page, by a filled-in worked example: 'Example: Total Advance Premium: $25,000 / Audit Noncompliance Charge Factor: 1 / Audit Noncompliance Charge: $25,000'. So page 256 offers an empty labelled box called 'Total Advance Premium' and, four lines below it, the string 'Total Advance Premium: $25,000' - on a policy whose GL advance premium is $3,954 and whose package total is $10,663. The page even labels it 'for illustration purposes only', which is the only thing standing between the extractor and a $25,000 premium. Note the factor '1' and the example both being 1 is coincidence, not corroboration.

_blank_form_trap.shared_lesson: FIVE separate forms in this one package print an empty schedule and point AWAY from themselves to the declarations - CA 21 50, CU 21 03, CG 72 76, CG 99 09 and (uncompleted rather than pointing) CA 8282. A retrieval filter that scores pages on 'does this look like a form with fields' keeps all five and can still lose every value they refer to. The one counter-example is IL 74 51 (pages 203 and 268), whose 'Description of Designated Operations' box IS filled in on the form itself - so 'exclusion forms have empty schedules' is not a rule either.
_blank_form_trap.the_asymmetry: An empty box costs nothing if it stays empty. The danger is entirely one-directional: these pages supply labels without values, and the pipeline's job is to resist supplying the value from somewhere else on the page. CG 99 09 is the only one that puts a plausible wrong value within four lines of the label.
